chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: Stuff Smith gets carried away in New York and the duo nights
summary: Stuff missed sets in New York, so Jones and Levy played as a duo, which led Webster, Byas and Hot Lips Page to hire them.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Uh-huh. You say Stuff changed and he

didn't mean to, but what was the change? How was he different? Just got -- how can you say he got carried away about something? He was in New York. When he was in Chicago we could handle him and hold him down, but when he got to New York, his cap came off again.
You know, he was -- he was a beautiful cat, a beautiful guy, you know, but he got back in New York and those big buildings got to him, I guess.
You, I think, said, another time when we were talking that he would sometimes miss the first two or three sets?
No, he just wouldn't show up. He'd come in there way late.
And so you and John had a duo those nights.

Yeah, we'd just play, just the two of us play, and they -- you know, that's a funny thing. That shows you how a negative situation, you can get something good out of it, and it did a lot for John and I.
Uh-huh. You had a whole new audience.
Yeah, we just went there and we were dressed, like I said, in our uniforms and on time, and that's
when Ben Webster and Don Byas and there was Hot Lips Page, too. So they began to hire us just like a rhythm section, you know?
